title: Burst Segmentation: an Approach for Reducing Packet Loss in Optical Burst- Switched Networks
problem: Whole bursts are dropped when two bursts contend at an OBS core node, wasting most of the data.
approach: Burst segmentation: split the burst and drop only the overlapping segments, combined with deflection routing.
finding: Dropping segments instead of whole bursts cuts packet loss compared with conventional burst dropping.

title: Generalized Burst Assembly and Scheduling Techniques for QoS Support in Optical Burst-Switched Networks
problem: OBS needs service differentiation without optical buffers.
approach: Generalized burst assembly and scheduling that places packets of different priority within a burst so low-priority segments are dropped first.
finding: Enables loss differentiation between traffic classes at the edge and core.

title: Prioritized Routing and Burst Segmentation for QoS in Optical Burst-Switched Networks
problem: Supporting QoS classes in OBS core nodes.
approach: Prioritized routing combined with burst segmentation, analyzed with a model checked against simulation.

title: Channel Scheduling Algorithms using Burst Segmentation and FDLs for Optical Burst-Switched Networks

approach: Scheduling algorithms that combine burst segmentation with fiber delay lines.
finding: Segmentation-aware scheduling lowers loss relative to scheduling without segmentation.

title: Dynamic Congestion-Based Load Balanced Routing in Optical Burst-Switched Networks

title: Early Drop Scheme for Providing Absolute QoS Differentiation in Optical Burst-Switched Networks

title: Early Drop and Wavelength Grouping Schemes for Providing Absolute QoS Differentiation in Optical Burst-Switched Networks

approach: Early drop combined with wavelength grouping that reserves channels per class.
finding: Both schemes bound high-priority loss independent of other classes' load.

title: Intermediate Node Initiated (INI) Signaling: A Hybrid Channel Reservation Technique for Optical Burst-Switched Networks

title: Prioritized Burst Segmentation and Composite Burst Assembly Techniques for QoS Support in Optical Burst-Switched Networks

title: Absolute QoS Differentiation in Optical Burst-Switched Networks

finding: Protection applicable across routing types with fewer resources.

title: Scheduled Lightpath Switching with Spatio-Spectral Resource Affinity
problem: Extreme-scale reservations leave fragmented time and spectrum unused.
approach: Scheduled lightpath switching with spatio-spectral resource affinity.
finding: Better use of fragmented resources raises utilization.

title: Using Machine Learning to Balance Energy Cost and Emissions in Optical Networks
problem: Minimizing electricity alone does not reduce environmental impact.
approach: Machine learning to balance energy cost and emissions in RWA (journal).
finding: Balances operating cost against emissions.

title: Failure-Aware Protection for Many-to-Many Routing in Content Centric Networks
problem: Disasters take out many links and nodes at once.
approach: Failure-aware protection for many-to-many routing using content-centric caching (journal).
finding: On-path caching plus precomputed backups improves reliability.

title: Light-segment: Crosstalk and Modulation-Aware Spectrum Allocation with Segmentation in SDM-EON
problem: Resource exhaustion in SDM elastic optical networks.
approach: Crosstalk- and modulation-aware spectrum allocation with request segmentation.
finding: Segmentation lowers blocking while respecting crosstalk limits.

title: Optimal PMU Restoration for Power System Observability Recovery After Massive Attacks
problem: Regaining grid situational awareness after massive cyber attacks.
approach: Optimal sequential restoration of PMUs (journal).
finding: Restoration order recovers observability quickly.

title: PMU and Communication Infrastructure Restoration for Post-Attack Observability Recovery of Power Grids
problem: Observability after attacks needs both PMUs and their communications back.
approach: Joint PMU and communication infrastructure restoration.
finding: Joint restoration recovers observability faster than restoring either alone.

title: A Cross-Domain Optimization Framework of PMU and Communication Placement for Multi-Domain Resiliency and Cost Reduction
problem: PMU placement and communication design are done separately.
approach: Cross-domain optimization of PMU and communication placement (journal).
finding: Improves multi-domain resiliency at lower cost.

title: Performance Comparison of Machine Learning Methods in DDoS Attack Detection in Smart Grids
problem: Detecting DDoS attacks in smart grids.
approach: Comparison of machine learning detectors.
finding: Identifies which methods detect DDoS best.

title: Static multi-sourced data retrieval in elastic optical networks
problem: Retrieving data held at several sources in EONs.
approach: Static multi-sourced data retrieval formulation and heuristics (journal).
finding: Efficient many-to-one retrieval plans.

title: A Scalable PDC Placement Technique for Fast and Resilient Monitoring of Large Power Grids
problem: Placing PDCs for fast, resilient monitoring of large grids.
approach: Scalable PDC placement technique (journal).
finding: Scales to large grids while keeping data transfer fast and resilient.

title: Cyber Restoration of Power Systems: Concept and Methodology for Resilient Observability
problem: Cyber attacks on wide-area monitoring blind operators.
approach: Cyber restoration concept and methodology for resilient observability (journal).
finding: Defines cyber restoration as a planning problem.

title: Disaster-Resilient PMU Network Design
problem: PMU networks must survive disasters.
approach: Disaster-resilient PMU network design.
finding: Designs that keep the grid observable after disasters.

title: PLI-Aware Dynamic Routing in Software Defined Elastic Optical Networks (SD- EONs)
problem: SDN controllers route without full physical-layer awareness.
approach: Load- and impairment-aware dynamic routing in SD-EONs.
finding: Considering all metrics together lowers blocking.

title: Situation-Aware Load Restoration Considering Uncertainty and Correlation
problem: Restoration after blackouts faces uncertain renewable and load patterns.
approach: Situation-aware load restoration with uncertainty and correlation (journal).
finding: More reliable restoration plans under uncertainty.

title: Cyber-Physical Reconfiguration for Disaster Resilience of Power Distribution Systems
problem: Cyber and power interdependence makes distribution systems fragile.
approach: Cyber-physical reconfiguration for disaster resilience.
finding: Joint reconfiguration speeds recovery.

title: PMU Network Routing for Resilient Observability of Power Grids
problem: Routing PMU data resiliently.
approach: PMU network routing for resilient observability.
finding: Routing that keeps the grid observable under failures.

title: Dynamic Crosstalk-Aware Routing, Modulation, Core, and Spectrum Allocation for Sliceable Demands in SDM-EONs
problem: Crosstalk limits SDM-EON capacity for sliceable demands.
approach: Dynamic crosstalk-aware routing, modulation, core, and spectrum allocation.
finding: Lower blocking within crosstalk thresholds.

title: Enhancing Routing in SD-EONs through Reinforcement Learning: A Comparative Analysis
problem: Static routing in SD-EONs cannot adapt to real-time conditions.
approach: Comparison of epsilon-greedy bandit, UCB bandit, and Q-learning routing.
finding: Reinforcement learning routing is compared against traditional methods in FUSION.

title: FUSION: A Flexible Unified Simulator for Intelligent Optical Networking
problem: Optical network simulators are mostly closed source.
approach: FUSION, an open-source simulator for software-defined elastic optical networks.
finding: Open, extensible platform adopted for the group's later studies.

title: Observability-Aware Resilient PMU Networking
problem: PMU networks must keep the grid observable under failures.
approach: Observability-aware resilient PMU networking framework (journal).
finding: Fast, resilient PMU data transfer.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Observability-Aware Cyber Restoration of Power Grid
problem: Cyber restoration is stochastic after disasters and attacks.
approach: Reinforcement learning for observability-aware cyber restoration.
finding: RL policies restore observability under uncertainty.

title: Best Planning Practices for Ultra-High-Capacity Networks Based on Multi- Band over Space Division Multiplexing
problem: Planners of ultra-high-capacity backbones must choose which bands to light and how much spatial multiplexing to add, and the choices interact through physical-layer impairments.
approach: A comparison of C, C+L, C+S, and C+L+S band plans over space-division multiplexed fiber under dynamic traffic, with quality of transmission modeled for each combination.
finding: C+L gives the best spectral efficiency, while C+L+S gives the most capacity and the lowest blocking, so the right plan depends on whether spectrum or throughput is the constraint.

title: Channel-Based ICXT- and NLI-Aware Service Provisioning for Multi-Band Over SDM Systems
problem: Bandwidth demand from 5G and beyond calls for multi-band transmission over space-division multiplexed fiber, but inter-core crosstalk, inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering, and fiber nonlinearity are intertwined there, and each varies with frequency.
approach: A channel-based resource allocation framework built on a generalized signal-to-noise ratio model that tracks frequency-dependent crosstalk and Raman scattering. Two allocation algorithms, Core-Spectrum-Band and Band-Spectrum-Core, are proposed for multi-core fiber and compared with bundled multi-fiber-pair architectures.
finding: Simulations on the U.S. backbone network show the approach significantly reduces blocking probability.

title: Cyber Security Constrained Economic Dispatch for Resilient Power System Operation
problem: Economic dispatch decides how to run generators at least cost, but it assumes the cyber network that carries measurements and controls is intact; a cyber contingency can make a cheap dispatch unsafe.
approach: An economic dispatch formulation with cyber security constraints, so that the schedule stays feasible and secure when parts of the communication and control network are compromised or lost.
finding: Dispatch that costs a little more in normal operation but remains secure under cyber contingencies that would violate the limits of a conventional dispatch.

title: Disaster-Resilient Cyber-Physical Distribution System Reconfiguration and Dynamic Networked Microgrid Formation under Intermittent Generation
problem: After a hurricane or other high-impact event, a distribution system has damaged lines, intermittent generation, and a communication network that may be down as well; restoring load quickly requires treating the power and communication layers together.
approach: A cyber-physical reconfiguration method that forms networked microgrids dynamically as conditions change, coordinating switching, distributed generation, and the communication paths the controls depend on.
finding: Faster load recovery than reconfiguration that ignores the communication layer, and reconfiguration that remains valid when generation is intermittent.

title: Exploring a Smart FDI Attack and Enhancing Anomaly Detection in Smart Meters
problem: Anomaly detection for smart meters usually watches power data alone, so a false-data-injection attack that stays consistent with the power data can pass unnoticed.
approach: Design of a smarter false-data-injection attack that respects the constraints existing detectors check, then an improved anomaly detector that uses more than the power measurements to catch it.
finding: The smarter attack evades existing detection, and the enhanced detector catches attacks the existing methods miss.

title: ISRS-Enhanced PLI-Aware Routing for Multi-Band Elastic Optical Networks
problem: Multi-band elastic optical networks add spectrum beyond the C-band, but amplifier noise, nonlinear interference, and inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering complicate dynamic allocation and degrade the quality of transmission.
approach: ISRS-Enhanced PLI-Aware (IE-PLIA) routing, which accounts for physical-layer impairments under the influence of Raman scattering and adjusts routing costs dynamically to each link's conditions and its self-channel and cross-channel interference.
finding: Routing that follows each link's interference conditions under Raman scattering, evaluated for dynamic multi-band allocation.

title: Learning to Slice: ML-Assisted Segmentation for Dynamic Resource Allocation in SDM-EONs
problem: Crosstalk-aware allocation in space-division multiplexed elastic optical networks slices demands across cores and spectrum, and the choice of slice size drives blocking; fixed rules pick it poorly under changing traffic.
approach: A machine-learning model inside the software-defined network controller that chooses the segmentation for each demand from the network state.
finding: Learned slicing lowers blocking compared with fixed segmentation rules.

title: Modeling Nonlinear Noise for Arbitrary Pulse Shapes in Optical Fiber Communication Systems
problem: Standard nonlinear noise models for fiber assume rectangular pulses, but real transmitters use shaped pulses, and the difference changes the noise a link accumulates.
approach: A modulation-format-dependent model of nonlinear noise that handles arbitrary pulse shapes, adding the terms that vanish only in the rectangular case.
finding: For non-rectangular pulses the additional nonlinear terms are significant, so quality-of-transmission estimates that assume rectangular pulses are optimistic.

title: QoS-Based Recovery in 6G Optical Transport Networks: A Fast Service Prioritization Approach
problem: 6G transport must restore mission-critical services fast.
approach: QoS-based service prioritization for recovery.
finding: Faster recovery for high-priority services.

title: Rethinking Flexibility: When Fixed-Grid with Grooming Outperforms Flex-Grid in EONs
problem: Is flex-grid always better than fixed-grid?
approach: Techno-economic comparison in super C-band SD-EONs, extending FUSION with grooming.
finding: Fixed-grid with grooming can outperform flex-grid.

title: Experimental Determination of Filter Bandwidth Requirements for Coherent Pluggable Transceivers in Optical Data Center Networks
problem: Coherent pluggable transceivers in data-center interconnects pass through cascaded ROADM filters, and each filter narrows the signal; too narrow a passband adds penalty, too wide wastes spectrum.
approach: Laboratory measurements of the passband needed by coherent pluggables as filter bandwidth is narrowed, to determine the smallest flexible-grid slot that keeps the penalty acceptable.
finding: Measured bandwidth requirements for coherent pluggables that flexible-grid ROADM planning can use directly, rather than rules of thumb.

title: FUSION: A Unified Benchmarking Framework for Reproducible Optical Network Research
problem: Results in optical networking are getting harder to compare and reproduce: architectures now range from single-band to multi-band and space-division systems, and published numbers depend on simulation assumptions that are rarely spelled out.
approach: FUSION treats the benchmark itself as the deliverable. It is organized around five pillars: verified baselines, coverage of the main functional domains, recorded experiment provenance and observability, extension through fixed interface contracts, and sustained ecosystem support. Reference scenarios, automated validation and regression workflows, and diagnostic outputs capture each run's configuration and state so it can be replayed deterministically.
finding: Case studies show the framework benchmarking heterogeneous architectures and policies on equal terms, and a mapping of published studies onto FUSION's capabilities shows how much of the field's recent work it can already reproduce.

title: QoT-Aware Dynamic Resource Allocation and Grooming in Multi-Band Space-Division Multiplexing Networks
problem: Multi-band space-division multiplexing can scale backbone capacity, but allocating resources dynamically means accounting for inter-core crosstalk, inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering, amplifier noise, and nonlinear interference at the same time, and their effects differ by band and by core count.
approach: A channel-based, quality-of-transmission-aware routing, modulation, core, band, and spectrum assignment framework that uses pre-computed generalized SNR and crosstalk feasibility maps over the C, L, and S bands, with end-to-end traffic grooming and bandwidth slicing built into the allocation. Two allocation orders, core-slot-band and band-slot-core, are compared on weakly coupled multi-core fibers and on bundles of standard single-mode fiber pairs.
finding: Ignoring frequency-dependent crosstalk causes systematic, band-dependent errors in which modulation formats are feasible in dense-core fibers. With few cores, multi-core fiber blocks less traffic than fiber bundles; with many cores, crosstalk dominates and bundles win. For seven cores, grooming pushes the onset of blocking to a 77.7 percent higher load, and the band-slot-core policy with grooming blocks 44.6 percent less than the bundle baseline across loads of 1,837 to 3,675 Tbps.

title: QoT-Aware Spectral and Spatial Scaling Trade-offs in Multi-Band Space Division Multiplexing over EONs [Invited]
problem: Backbone capacity can grow two ways, by adding bands beyond the C-band or by adding fiber cores, and physical-layer impairments mean the two cannot be judged separately: the L-band suffers more crosstalk, and dense cores make crosstalk dominate.
approach: A planning framework that jointly evaluates C, C+L, C+S, and C+L+S transmission over 4-, 7-, 13-, and 19-core fibers, using one generalized SNR model that covers amplifier noise, nonlinear interference, stimulated Raman scattering, inter-core crosstalk, transceiver limits, and filtering and aging penalties. Modulation formats are pre-computed with launch-power optimization and bandwidth slicing, and the crosstalk model is validated on a commercial 19-core fiber.
finding: The best band plan depends on the core count. C+L wins for 4 and 7 cores; C+S wins for 13 cores because the L-band is hit harder by crosstalk; at 19 cores the system is crosstalk-dominated and only C+S holds up. Adding cores can shrink usable capacity: with C+L+S, maximum throughput falls from 107.94 Pbps at 13 cores to 44.76 Pbps at 19 on the U.S. backbone topology.
